source.title: A Robust Initialization of Residual Blocks for Effective ResNet Training Without Batch Normalization
source.authors: Enrico Civitelli; Alessio Sortino; Matteo Lapucci; Francesco Bagattini; G. Galvan

record.file_problem: None; full paper text including appendices is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports natural-label train and test performance for normalization-free ResNets using a modified residual architecture and initialization, a setting not covered by the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports train/test accuracy and signal-propagation measurements. It does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks, the mapped optimizer/batch-size/dropout comparisons, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Comparisons with prior work are not extracted as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study tests normalization-free residual architectures and initialization schemes. Its natural-label accuracy and signal-propagation results do not test any of V1–V8. Reporting held-out accuracy alone does not test the specific generalization comparisons those versions describe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that modified residual summation with suitable initialization enables competitive normalization-free ResNet training on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. They acknowledge potentially slower training and a possible need for strong augmentation to replace BatchNorm's regularization; their experiments use RandAugment and, on ImageNet, label smoothing.
record.recipe_differences: Changes residual-block summation and initialization; uses SGD and data augmentation, with no batch normalization in the proposed setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance and trainability vary with residual summation and initialization scheme, network depth, dataset, and training duration; stronger data augmentation may be needed without batch normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: ConvShort with the proposed initialization closes the BatchNorm accuracy gap on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; ImageNet performance is described as competitive against an externally reported standard ResNet-50 baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitable residual summation and initialization can enable normalization-free ResNets to achieve competitive image-classification accuracy with the reported augmentation recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed initialization preserves backward signal variance, whereas the tested Brock initialization configurations exhibit exploding gradients and fail to train ResNet-50 and ResNet-101.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backward signal preservation at initialization affects trainability of deep normalization-free residual networks.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems (venue stated in supplied metadata); paper text identifies itself as a preprint.
record.problems: Train/test accuracy values are presented in plots without numeric values in the supplied text; ImageNet comparison uses accuracy reported by PyTorch for a standard ResNet-50 rather than a matched run described here. Results are means and standard deviations of three runs for the CIFAR-10 experiments; uncertainty for other reported comparisons is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for other plotted CIFAR-10 configurations using Brock et al. initialization or the remaining batch-normalized and proposed variants' signal-propagation curves, because their plotted values are figure-only and the text does not state separate outcomes for each. ResNet-18 curves are also figure-only; the text only says it can be trained using all considered initializations.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance, paired with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width variation beyond the threshold for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout addition or removal, including its interaction with weight decay and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern findings outside the supplied versions and should not serve as claim-verdict evidence. Figure curves are unavailable in the supplied text, so exact accuracies cannot be recovered. The citation to Hoffer et al. concerns BatchNorm regularization and supplies no original batch-size comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare random-label and natural-label generalization.
Compares depths and residual configurations, not width beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
No fully connected image-network comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
Uses SGD; does not compare adaptive optimizers.
Uses batch size 128 (100 for ImageNet); no large- versus small-batch comparison.
Does not compare dropout or its removal.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare generalization measures.
Does not remove or retrain on memorized examples.
